Windows chat now includes a checksum-verified Vulkan GPU runtime alongside the CPU fallback. The desktop launcher no longer forces the CPU executable. Uncloud selects the GPU backend when it reports a usable device; an explicit custom runtime still takes precedence. Graphics-driver support is required.

Compatible native GGUF runtimes now fit context and offload placement using llama.cpp’s actual model/cache memory accounting. The displayed window comes from the running backend, instead of being capped again by Uncloud’s dense FP16 estimate. CPU fitting also protects RAM already used by other applications. This does not guarantee a particular context size on every machine.

Custom context Apply reloads the model and displays the allocated window and model maximum. Leaving the field blank and applying resets Auto. Invalid values are rejected before unloading the resident model. Switching text models waits for the old process to exit, including after a forced stop, before starting its replacement.

Chat now manages a rolling context automatically near 75% of the allocated window. Older exchanges are summarized while recent turns stay in context. Every original message remains in the encrypted conversation. Compatible native models can use the neutral `conversation_search` tool to recall earlier messages, independently of Web; other backends receive locally matched excerpts when relevant. Retrieval uses no second model and never searches another conversation. If a summary fails, a measured recent window keeps the conversation going and the UI reports that older messages remain saved for recall. A single oversized latest message or retained memory can still exceed the supported window.

Compaction now uses a cancellable stream with a 90-second overall deadline and repeated-thinking detection, instead of waiting up to 15 minutes per response. Empty, cut-off or non-shrinking summaries are not applied. Automatic preparation attempts at most two summaries and does not retry a failed one. Summary and recall are lossy and relevance-dependent; they do not enlarge the model's native context or guarantee perfect memory.

GGUF replies are bounded to the loaded context instead of allowing unlimited context shifting. Sustained exact reasoning cycles stop with an error and preserve the conversation. Auto thinking, native samplers and tool templates are unchanged; no identity, date or persona instructions are added. Web evidence fitting no longer uses its fitting reserve as an automatic reply ceiling. These safeguards do not guarantee that every model will produce a final answer.

Settings now lists models held across text, image, video, cached transcription, voice and narration modules, with worker/job activity. The text row includes runtime device information and allocated context. Unload all also clears cached voice and narration models. The Guide and installation notes explain the behavior.

Validation: 1,130 backend tests passed (3 skipped), 201 frontend tests passed, and the production build, Python lint and release-resource checks passed. Coverage includes native context fitting, custom reload/Auto reset, model-stop ordering, runtime selection, resident inventory, summary deadlines/cancellation, multi-tool evidence fitting, and continuation with original-message recall after a failed summary. On the already-loaded Qwen3.5 9B MLX model, a synthetic continuity summary completed in 4.29 seconds and a native conversation-search/answer round completed in 3.24 seconds; no additional model was loaded. Windows GPU execution and large-context performance still require physical Windows hardware verification.
